questions.prompt: What does how to win mean in this chapter?
choices: Choosing why the offer should be preferred on the chosen field
Promising to work harder than every competitor
Listing every attractive feature in the category

explanation.gentle: The chapter treats how to win as the reason a customer should prefer the offer, not as a promise of effort.
explanation.direct: How to win defines the advantage or value equation that should beat alternatives on the selected field.
explanation.competitive: The right answer names the edge. The other two only add noise.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter use Glad ForceFlex?
choices: To argue that every strategy should rely on head-to-head imitation
To show that stronger offer logic can improve a business
To prove that customer preference never changes

explanation.gentle: Glad ForceFlex matters because it shows how-to-win as a real choice about value.
explanation.direct: The example demonstrates that a more compelling offer logic can strengthen the business more than generic competitive intensity can.
explanation.competitive: Glad works here because the edge got sharper, not because the company got louder.

questions.prompt: A team says it will win by being better, faster, and more innovative than everyone else. What is the clearest diagnosis?
choices: The team has already named a full value equation
The team is still describing virtues instead of a real reason to choose the offer
The team has proven head-to-head comparison is the best route

explanation.gentle: Those claims can sound strong, but they still may not explain why customers should choose the offer.
explanation.direct: This is virtue language without a defined basis of preference, so the how-to-win choice is still incomplete.
explanation.competitive: The team is flexing intensity because it still cannot name the edge.

questions.prompt: Leila's launch deck shows twelve matched competitor checkboxes. What should she ask next?
choices: Which exact reason should make the target customer prefer the offer?
How can the team add even more parity boxes to the slide?
Which rival slogan sounds strongest for imitation?

explanation.gentle: Leila needs to move from parity evidence to the actual reason customers should choose the offer.
explanation.direct: Matching the competitor list does not define the value equation. She has to name the basis of preference.
explanation.competitive: Parity is not the edge. The real question is why anyone should pick them.

questions.prompt: What is the best distinction between differentiation language and a real how-to-win choice?
choices: Differentiation language avoids making any claim about customer value
A real how-to-win choice makes the basis of customer preference explicit
There is no difference if the team sounds confident

explanation.gentle: The chapter wants the strategy to explain why customers should choose it, not just sound distinctive.
explanation.direct: A real how-to-win choice specifies the value equation behind preference instead of relying on vague difference claims.
explanation.competitive: Confidence does not rescue blur. The edge has to become visible.

questions.prompt: Why can head-to-head competition be a trap?
choices: Because direct comparison may force the company onto the rival's strongest terms
Because customers dislike all comparisons
Because every rival-defined market should be abandoned immediately

explanation.gentle: The rival may already be strongest on those comparison terms, which makes direct imitation risky.
explanation.direct: Head-to-head can be weak strategy when it accepts a basis of comparison that favors the competitor.
explanation.competitive: If the rival owns the scoreboard, marching onto it is bad design.

questions.prompt: Sumi says her tutoring project will succeed because she will work harder than everyone else. What is missing?
choices: A reason families should prefer her offer over alternatives
A bigger list of tutoring subjects
A longer explanation of how disciplined she is

explanation.gentle: Hard work matters, but families still need a clear reason to choose the offer.
explanation.direct: The missing piece is the value equation for the chosen audience, not another statement about effort.
explanation.competitive: Stamina is not yet a win path. Preference still has to be designed.

questions.prompt: Dante's company compares itself directly on a rival's strongest low-cost terms. What is the best next move?
choices: Accept the rival's comparison and intensify the same argument
Test whether another basis of value creates stronger preference on the chosen field
Remove all pricing discussion and hope the issue disappears

explanation.gentle: A different comparison can be stronger when the current one favors the rival too much.
explanation.direct: The chapter encourages testing another basis of preference instead of blindly accepting the rival's easiest terms.
explanation.competitive: Change the game before you keep losing on their turf.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's main limit on alternate win paths?
choices: They are only allowed in consumer brands
They work only when buyers value them enough to change preference
They should always avoid any direct comparison at all

explanation.gentle: A different route still has to matter to customers before it counts.
explanation.direct: Novelty becomes strategy only when it creates believable customer preference rather than just a fresher internal story.
explanation.competitive: If buyers do not care, the clever route is still dead.

questions.prompt: Once a company names its how-to-win choice clearly, what question does the next chapter naturally raise?
choices: How can it add more generic competitive adjectives?
What capabilities are required to make that edge real?
How can it postpone delivery until the market softens?

explanation.gentle: A named edge still has to be supported by what the organization can actually do.
explanation.direct: The next strategic step is to identify the capabilities required to deliver the chosen advantage credibly.
explanation.competitive: Once the edge is named, execution fitness becomes the next pressure test.
